title: Docs: incident bot responder guide + `context` request command examples
author: Jacob Stein
description:
This PR updates on-call documentation for the incident bot context bundles and adds concrete examples for requesting *additional* context during triage (without waiting on another bot auto-post). Motivation: responders asked for a single canonical place to learn (a) what the bot posts by default, (b) how to request a deeper bundle, and (c) how restricted-mode affects what gets posted in #incidents vs restricted channels.

Key changes: (1) Add a responder-facing guide under /docs/oncall that explains the default bundle order, time windows, and what “fail-open” looks like when a collector times out. (2) Add a “How to request additional context” section with copy/paste Slack command examples. (3) Link the doc to the Confluence runbook so responders can go from “suspected change” evidence → decision tree (rollback/disable flag/revert routing) quickly.

Slack command examples included in docs (exact strings): `@redwood-incident-bot help context` (lists available options), `@redwood-incident-bot context --window=60m` (re-run bundle with a wider window), `@redwood-incident-bot context --collectors=deploy,config` (limit scope to reduce noise), `@redwood-incident-bot context --include-links=true` (ensure dashboard/runbook links are attached), and `@redwood-incident-bot context --mode=restricted` (when in a customer-sensitive incident; posts minimal metadata in #incidents and full bundle to the configured restricted channel).

Notes/guardrails documented: timeouts are hard-capped per collector; requesting more context should be used intentionally to avoid thread spam; never paste customer payloads/tokens; if a bundle section shows `redacted` the responder should follow the runbook to fetch details via approved tools.

Confluence runbook link added (internal): https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ONCALL/pages/2290419712/Runbook+Triage+with+Deploy+and+Config+Context

Testing: docs build + link checker; no runtime code changes.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): we should mirror the responder guide into Confluence for searchability, but keep GitHub docs as source-of-truth for versioned command strings.
commits: docs(oncall): add incident bot responder guide + context bundle overview
docs: add request-more-context command examples + restricted-mode notes
docs: link Confluence triage runbook + add troubleshooting/FAQ
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher: Can we add one explicit note about what to do when a collector section errors (metrics lag / timeouts), so responders don’t assume “no data == no issue”? Also include the default window (last 30m) since folks keep guessing.

Jacob Stein (author): Added a “When a collector fails” subsection with the exact wording used in partial bundle rendering, plus the default window and how to widen it.

Marissa Cole: The command examples are good but a little long in the first screen. Can we move the more advanced flags under a collapsible / “advanced” heading and keep the top section to 2–3 common cases?

Jacob Stein (author): Reordered: top section is `help context`, `context --window=60m`, and `context --collectors=deploy,config`. Advanced flags moved to a later heading.

Marcus Lin: Please be careful with the restricted-mode guidance: avoid implying responders should manually post anything sensitive. Also call out that restricted mode is channel-configured/allowlisted and doesn’t override Slack permissions.

Jacob Stein (author): Updated restricted-mode section: clarified that the bot uses channel allowlists, posts minimal metadata in #incidents, and responders should use approved internal tools for deeper investigation; added a line that restricted mode does not grant additional access.

Rafael Mendes: LGTM once the Confluence link is added and the doc points to the runbook decision tree. Also add a quick FAQ entry for “bot posted too much / too noisy” → how to give feedback.

Jacob Stein (author): Added Confluence runbook link and an FAQ entry that points to the feedback channel + Linear issue template.

Marissa Cole: Approved.
Sean Gallagher: Approved.
Marcus Lin: Approved after last edit.

Merged via squash.
release_notes: On-call docs now include copy/paste Slack commands for requesting additional incident-bot context bundles, plus updated guidance on restricted-mode and collector failure interpretation.
